long_biography.plain_text:
Trained as a mechanical engineer in Denmark, Thottrup spent roughly a decade in engineering before moving into British construction. In 1993 he became an entrepreneur, developing and restoring high-end London properties through P&N companies. That work gave him the technical and spatial experience to tackle complex historic buildings.

In 2001 he and Jeanette bought a neglected estate near Siena, initially imagining a private home. Seven years of restoration turned Borgo Santo Pietro into a boutique hotel built around gardens, farming, food and highly personal service. Thottrup remains closely involved in design, construction and operations as the group extends its approach across restaurants, private residences, skincare and other carefully connected businesses.

uncertainties.detail: The first-party Satori and Borgo sites, RINA interview, regulatory admission document and Companies House record all converge on the same Danish property developer resident in Italy. The regulatory ownership structure directly connects the Thottrups' holding company to the 41.5-metre vessel. No facts from unrelated Thottrup family members or similarly named people are transferred.

The authoritative relationship begins in 2014, while public sources describe Satori's design and construction before its 2017 launch. The regulatory document traces ownership through Borgo Lifestyle Finance and Big Blue Cruising, and RINA calls Thottrup co-owner. The dossier treats the public and authoritative dates as different stages of the same project and excludes the yacht from the biographies.

Verified Companies House data establishes August 1963 and aligns exactly with the authoritative record's calculated age of 56 on 7 May 2020. Reliable sources do not publish the day. One lower-tier article names Copenhagen as his birthplace, but that is insufficient for a place_of_birth proposal.

The regulatory biography proves that Thottrup moved from employment into founder-built property companies and later co-created Borgo Santo Pietro. It does not describe his family wealth, launch capital or financial backing. The broader Self-made category is therefore used rather than inferring either an independent or materially advantaged start.

Real Estate is the wealth-creation industry because the London P&N property companies preceded and enabled the Tuscan project. Hospitality is the current primary industry because Thottrup's defining public role is leading Borgo Santo Pietro Group's hotel, restaurant and guest businesses. PN Homes remains active but does not erase the shift in principal public operating focus.

The official Borgo Santo Pietro site is proposed as the current Company Website because it directly names the founders. No exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website or dedicated Forbes profile could be verified strongly enough for proposal. Company-level social accounts are not misrepresented as personal profiles.

Property developer and Luxury hospitality are the minimum useful approved active tags because both are defining, long-running practiced roles supported by operating control. Mechanical engineer is formative but not current and the catalogue lacks a need to duplicate education. Yacht designer would overgeneralise from an isolated project, so it is omitted.

The biographies cover engineering, London property development, the Tuscan transformation and the integrated hospitality model. Satori, bond financing, ownership percentages, room counts, acreage, restaurant awards, revenue, valuations and personal net worth are deliberately excluded.
